<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 126|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIIII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=14|verse=31}} But he {{ls}}pake more vehemently, Although I {{ls}}hould die together vvith thee, I vvil not denie thee. And in like maner al{{ls}}o {{ls}}aid they al.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=32}} And they come into a farme-place called Geth{{ls}}emani. And he {{ls}}aith to his Di{{ls}}ciples, Sit you here, vntil I pray. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=33}} And he taketh Peter and Iames and Iohn vvith him: and he began to feare and to be heauy. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=34}} And he {{ls}}aith to them, My {{ls}}oul is {{ls}}orovvful euen vnto death: {{ls}}tay here, and vvatch. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=35}} And vvhen he vvas gone forvvard a litle, he fel flat vpon the ground: and he prayed that if it might be, the houre might pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e from him: {{verse|chapter=14|verse=36}} and he {{ls}}aid, Abba, Father, al things are po{{ls}}sible to thee, tran{{ls}}ferre this chalice from me. but not that vvhich I vvil, but that vvhich thou. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=37}} And he commeth, and findeth them {{ls}}leeping. And he {{ls}}aith to Peter, Simon, {{ls}}leepe{{ls}}t thou? could{{ls}}t thou not vvatch one houre? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=38}} VVatch ye, and pray that you enter not into tentation. The {{ls}}pirit in deede is prompt, but the fle{{ls}}h infirme. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=39}} And going avvay againe, he prayed, {{ls}}aying the {{ls}}elf{{ls}}ame vvord. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=40}} And returning, againe he found them a {{ls}}leepe (for their eies vvere heauy) and they vvi{{ls}}t not vvhat they {{ls}}hould an{{ls}}vver him. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=41}} And he commeth the third time, and {{ls}}aith to them, Sleepe ye novv, and take re{{ls}}t, it {{ls}}uffi{{ls}}eth, the houre is come: behold the Sonne of man {{ls}}hal be betraied into the hands of {{ls}}inners. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=42}} Ari{{ls}}e, let vs goe. behold, he that {{ls}}hal betray me, is at hand.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=43}} And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 47. Luc. 22, 47. Io. 18, 3.''}}* as he vvas yet {{ls}}peaking, commeth Iudas I{{ls}}cariote one of the Tvvelue, and vvith him a great multitude vvith {{ls}}vvordes and clubbes, from the cheefe Prie{{ls}}tes and the Scribes and the Auncients. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=44}} And the betrayer of him had giuen them a {{ls}}igne, {{ls}}aying, VVhom{{ls}}oeuer I {{ls}}hal ki{{ls}}{{ls}}e, it is he, lay hold on him, and leade him vvarily. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=45}} And vvhen he vvas come, immediatly going to him, he {{ls}}aith, Rabbi, and he ki{{ls}}{{ls}}ed him. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=46}} But they laid hands vpon him: and held him. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=47}} And one certaine man of the {{ls}}tāders about, dravving out a {{ls}}vvord, {{ls}}mote the {{ls}}eruant of the cheefe prie{{ls}}t, and cut of his eare. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=48}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid to them, As to a theefe are you come out vvith {{ls}}vvordes and clubbes to apprehend me? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=49}} I vvas daily vvith you in the temple teaching, and you did not lay hands on me. But, that the Scriptures may be fulfilled. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=50}} Then his di{{ls}}ciples leauing him, al fled. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=51}} And a certaine yong man folowed him clothed vvith {{ls}}indon vpō the bare: & they tooke him. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=52}} But he ca{{ls}}ting of the {{ls}}indon, fled from them naked.
